subtitle: Spain edges France as the narrow leader in the 2026 World Cup winner market thanks to La Roja’s status as European champions and a deep squad featuring Lamine Yamal, whose potential return from a hamstring injury has stabilized their implied probability near 17 percent. France sits just behind, buoyed by longstanding depth and Didier Deschamps’ experience, while England benefits from back-to-back major final appearances. Brazil and Argentina maintain strong positioning as South American powers with proven tournament pedigree, and Portugal rounds out the tightly bunched group. This competitive balance stems from multiple sides possessing elite talent, solid recent form, and no single dominant narrative, keeping the top probabilities clustered within a few percentage points.
